lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet can be revealing in hockey, and Toronto's silence this September says plenty - the Maple Leafs are trying to steady the ship from the blue line out. Morgan Rielly's public embrace of Toronto as "my home" is the most encouraging note of camp, because this club badly needs its longest-serving defenceman to look anchored, not hunted. Dakota Joshua's unnamed injury is the nagging headache, with his opener status still uncertain, while Philippe Myers suddenly has a path to matter if he can turn a deep-offseason afterthought into a useful depth story. The Leafs are not chasing a standings fight now; they're building a roster. That starts with health, roles, and a cleaner support cast. Watch the final preseason tune-up and the opening-night roster decisions - they'll tell us who has survived the cut.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The calendar says offseason, but the Blue Jays are still living with the wreckage of a brutal finish - and a front office that now has to make sense of it. Dylan Cease's MRI brought the one piece of comfort in the pile: inflammation, not surgery, and that keeps a rotation cornerstone on the board for 2027. That matters because Toronto's pitching picture is already frayed, with rookie Trey Yesavage back from the injured list and Brett Bateman knocked from the lineup by right hip discomfort. The Jays have also shuffled the deck with Chad Dallas up, Joe Mantiply gone, and Michael Lorenzen testing free agency, all while the club's final record - 76-86 - tells the ugly truth. Now comes the winter's real test: whether this roster gets repaired or merely rearranged.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet is not a bad thing in late September - it means the roster is settling, and the paperwork is finally catching up to the summer's intentions. Jaden Bradley has been elevated to a standard deal and Malachi Smith has taken the open two-way slot, a tidy bit of housekeeping that says Toronto has chosen development with a little more conviction than usual. The numbers are plain enough: Bradley, the 50th pick, is in; Smith, fresh off 15 games with Brooklyn last season, gets another runway. That leaves Jakob Poeltl as the old pro in the room - the pivot point for a team that still needs sturdier paint play and cleaner possessions. Training camp opens Sept. 29 in Quebec City, and that is where the next argument begins.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The alarm bell in Washington is not about the calendar - it's about the quarterback's elbow, again. Jayden Daniels will consult specialists this week after dislocating his left, non-throwing elbow, and that's the kind of injury that forces an offseason to turn sharp and ugly in a hurry. The Commanders' season is over, officially in the books, and now the work is all about protection, contingency and patience. Daniels is the franchise, but a franchise is only as sturdy as the plan around him, and right now the plan is being stress-tested by pain and uncertainty. Dan Quinn has to manage the message, the roster and the medical truth at once - no easy trick. What to watch next: the specialist reports, the backup QB hierarchy, and whether Washington's front can build real insurance before camp opens.

article.title: Tuesday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs are spending this stretch on two familiar questions: whether Philippe Myers can carve out a useful 2026-27 role, and how the club can rekindle Morgan Rielly, who Sportsnet framed as part of the team's push to get him moving again. The Blue Jays are still carrying the sting of that late loss, with Sportsnet saying Yariel Yesavage's return got overshadowed as Toronto's playoff hopes took another hit.

For the Raptors, attention is turning to Jakob Poeltl and whether he can get back to form in the season where the team needs him most, alongside a look at how Toronto fits in the revamped Eastern Conference. In Washington, the Commanders are watching college options in "Future Hogs" while pressure keeps building around Jayden Daniels' injury and Dan Quinn's hot seat chatter.
